purpose: Brand entry point; routes users to the commercial sections, Bespoke and Education.
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 1] homepage exists. [STAGE 10] OV-13: homepage title targets 'Lab-Grown Diamond Engagement Rings', the same subject as /engagement-rings (POSSIBLE_OVERLAP, title level only).
current_issue: Homepage title competes on subject with /engagement-rings (OV-13).
notes: INFERENCE: the homepage should target the brand and the overall offer, and leave category-level subjects to their category pages. Final title/keyword targeting is Stage 15.

purpose: Primary commercial hub for engagement rings; parent of style subcategories and of the engagement-ring product set.
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 1] largest product group (~74 of 169 PDP slugs are engagement-ring related; slug-derived, approximate). [STAGE 1] sitemap category. [STAGE 11] CL-120/121/122/124 in area 1. [STAGE 8] the only validated engagement-ring style query (side stones engagement rings) is CATEGORY-dominant and TRANSACTIONAL.
current_issue: Template meta description ('Browse {X} from the live catalog') [STAGE 1]; subject overlap with homepage title [STAGE 10 OV-13].
notes: OBSERVED FACT: the master keyword DB holds no measured head term for 'engagement rings' or lab-grown engagement rings (0 matches for lab+engagement patterns in the Stage 11 map). The hub's place rests on catalogue share and the business context, not measured volume. That is a keyword-data gap, not evidence of no demand.

purpose: Style-led landing page for side-stone engagement rings.
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 3] only subcategory URL with a ranking (side stones engagement rings, pos 104, vol 1,000). [STAGE 8] SERP CATEGORY-dominant/TRANSACTIONAL; competitors rank style category pages, 3 nested under an engagement-rings parent (helzberg.com/engagement-rings/side-stone, diamondsfactory.com/engagement-rings/side-stone-rings, sarahojewelry /collections/engagement-rings/ring-style-side-stone; zales uses a flat side-stones-engagement-rings). [STAGE 10] SERP ALIGNMENT row; OV-17 parent/child DISTINCT. [STAGE 11] CL-120.
current_issue: Not in sitemap; misspelled intermediate segment 'by-desgin' [STAGE 10].
notes: The only style subcategory with direct SERP evidence that Google serves a category page for the query. The URL/migration question is not decided here.

section: Engagement Rings > Style subcategories (Solitaire, Halo, Pavé, Three-Stone, Bezel, Toi-et-Moi, Nature-Inspired)
purpose: Style-led landing pages for the other ring styles HOD already merchandises.
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 10] 7 live style URLs besides side-stone (plus the /by-desgin hub), all populated (approx. 1–24 product links each), none in sitemap, none ranking. [STAGE 8] side-stone evidence shows the style-subcategory pattern is how Google serves at least one style query. [STAGE 11] no keyword cluster for these styles (keyword-data gap). CL-121 'types of diamond settings' is an EDITORIAL_GUIDE SERP, i.e. an informational need, not a category need.
current_equivalent: /engagement-rings/by-desgin/{bezel-rings, halo-ring, nature-inspired-rings, pave, solitare-rings, three-stone-rings, toi-moi-rings}
current_issue: Not in sitemap; misspellings (by-desgin, solitare); inconsistent naming (halo-ring singular vs *-rings plural; toi-moi vs toi-et-moi used for necklaces) [STAGE 10].
notes: Style is a real merchandising dimension, so style subcategories are a valid page type. Each style is indexable only if it passes the Facet/Subcategory Gate (decision log D-07): measured demand + category-type SERP + enough products + distinct from parent. Style demand was not measured in project data.

section: Engagement Rings > Diamond shape (round, oval, pear, emerald, radiant, marquise, heart, princess, cushion, asscher)
purpose: Let buyers narrow the engagement-ring set by centre-stone shape.
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 1] shape tokens appear in many PDP slugs (round 40, oval 19, emerald 17, pear 17, radiant 12, marquise 12, heart 11 ...; slug-derived). [STAGE 11] 0 shape+jewellery-type keywords in the master map. [STAGE 8] shape SERPs observed are informational ('diamond shape' = EDITORIAL_GUIDE) or loose-diamond/brand ('asscher cut diamond'), and 1 PRODUCT SERP ('marquise oval diamond', where HOD's PDP ranks at pos 90).
current_equivalent: No shape landing pages exist; shapes appear only in product slugs.
current_issue: None structural; the data gap is the issue.
notes: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — DEFER for shape landing pages. Shape-led engagement-ring queries were not in the keyword universe (Stage 4/6 seeding was domain- and lab-grown-led), so demand is unmeasured, not absent. Shape is a filter by default until a targeted commercial keyword pull and SERP check are done.

purpose: Let buyers narrow by stone origin inside the engagement-ring set.
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 10] homepage title targets 'Lab-Grown Diamond Engagement Rings'. [STAGE 11] 0 master keywords combine lab-grown/natural with engagement ring. [STAGE 8] origin head terms alone ('lab grown diamonds', 'natural diamonds') are served by retailer collection pages.
current_issue: Origin is not exposed as a navigable dimension.
notes: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — DEFER on a 'lab-grown engagement rings' landing page. It is the most plausible attribute landing page given the business model and the homepage positioning, but project data has no measurement for it. It needs a commercial keyword pull + SERP check before Stage 15.

section: Engagement Rings > Metal / Carat / Price / Setting height and other attributes

Price keywords: 9, all informational ('are lab grown diamonds cheaper'). Carat keywords are loose-diamond or suitability questions (CL-006, CL-049), not ring-category queries.

purpose: Commercial hub for wedding and anniversary bands.

current_issue: Most of the subcategory layer is empty; template meta description.
notes: Retained as an L1 section on business context (bridal is core to a diamond-ring business) and existing structure. Demand is unmeasured, not absent.

purpose: Split bands by wearer where the product sets genuinely differ.
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 10] /wedding-bands/for-her populated (~7 links); /wedding-bands/for-him and all 3 of its children empty. [STAGE 11] 2 gender keywords, both informational ('are mens and womens ring sizes the same', 'do men get engagement rings too').
current_issue: Men's branch is empty but live and linked in nav.
notes: Gender is a legitimate top split for bands, but a branch with no products should not exist as an indexable page (principle P-EMPTY). Demand unmeasured.

section: Wedding Bands > Band style (eternity, anniversary, pavé, solid, classic, designer, diamond, cigar, nature)
purpose: Style refinement within bands.

current_issue: 7 of 9 empty; misspellings (anniversay, pavee); eternity duplicated across two parents.
notes: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — DEFER on which band styles become indexable. Structural principle only: one product type has one category home (eternity bands live in one place), and gender-by-style combinations are filters unless gated.

purpose: Umbrella parent for non-bridal jewellery types (earrings, necklaces & pendants, bracelets, rings).
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 1] sitemap category. [STAGE 10] parent of 21 nav subcategory URLs. [STAGE 11] 0 master keywords for 'fine jewellery' (keyword-data gap). [STAGE 11 map] US spelling: 'jewelry' appears in 23 master keywords, 'jewellery' in 1.
current_issue: Template meta description; the umbrella label has no measured search role; British spelling in a US-primary market.
notes: Kept as the umbrella because (a) it already exists and parents the live earrings/necklaces/bracelet URLs, and (b) no evidence shows a flatter structure would do better. Whether the label or slug uses 'jewelry' is a deferred migration question (D-15).

purpose: Commercial category for all earrings.
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 1] second-largest product group (~40 PDP slugs; approximate). [STAGE 10] live at /fine-jewellery/earrings (~24+ links), not in sitemap. current_issue: Not in sitemap; Stage 1 missed it.

purpose: Earring type landing pages.

purpose: Commercial category for necklaces and pendants.

current_issue: Not in sitemap; label says 'Necklaces' but pendants are a child type; T-Bar sits outside the hierarchy.
notes: Section name combines necklaces and pendants to match how the catalogue is merchandised. Naming is not keyword-validated.

notes: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — DEFER on whether T-Bar is a necklace subtype, a curated collection or neither. Principle: a style collection should not sit beside product-type categories at L1 unless it has independent demand.

purpose: Commercial category for bracelets.
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 1] ~10 bracelet PDP slugs (approximate). [STAGE 10] live at /fine-jewellery/bracelet (~11 links), not in sitemap. [STAGE 11] no cluster (keyword-data gap); bracelet keywords in the master DB are brand or metal-wear questions.

purpose: Bracelet type landing pages.

[STAGE 8] 'mixed metal ring' (4,400) and 'morganite rings' (8,100) are CATEGORY SERPs, but HOD's catalogue fit for them is not established. [STAGE 1] ~14 'ring' PDP slugs not matched to bridal patterns (approximate).
current_issue: Nearly empty; overlaps bridal bands.
notes: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — DEFER on the scope of this category. The category exists as a structural slot; what belongs in it depends on catalogue decisions outside SEO data.

purpose: Commercial landing page for lab-grown diamond jewellery (and loose stones if offered); links out to Education for 'what/how/vs' questions.
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 8] 'lab grown diamonds' (135,000) and 'lab diamonds' (27,100) SERPs are retailer collection/category pages (withclarity /collections/lab-diamonds, brilliantearth /lab-grown-diamonds/, miadonna /collections/lab-grown-diamond-jewelry, stienhardt /collections/...). [STAGE 11] CL-001 MIXED/HIGH evidence; DISTINCT_INTENT from CL-002 definitional. [STAGE 10] no HOD URL matches the head terms; HOD's lab-grown equity is all in informational blog posts.

current_issue: No commercial landing page for the business's core stone type.
notes: Google treats the head term as commercial, so an informational article cannot be the primary answer. Condition: the business confirms lab-grown is the primary catalogue positioning (the homepage title suggests so) and the page holds real product inventory. Education remains the home for CL-002 to CL-023 informational needs.

purpose: Commercial landing page for natural diamond jewellery, if HOD sells it.
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 8] 'natural diamonds' (18,100) and 'natural mined diamonds' SERPs are retailer pages (solomonbrothers /natural-diamonds, withclarity /collections/natural-diamonds, diamondsdirect /natural-diamonds/). [STAGE 11] CL-070 HIGH. [STAGE 1] no PDP slug indicates natural stones; the business context says HOD sells or promotes natural diamonds.
current_issue: Whether natural-diamond products exist in the catalogue is not visible in project data.
notes: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — DEFER. The page type is justified by the SERP, but only if HOD actually sells natural-diamond pieces. That is a business question, not an SEO-data question.

purpose: Explains and sells the custom/commission service; lead capture.

section: Curated / merchandising collections (e.g. Hip Hop, gifts, new-in)

current_issue: Placeholder and test artifact on a live URL.

purpose: One page per sellable product; variants (carat, metal, size) selected on-page.
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 1] 169 PDPs under flat /shop/<slug>; 3 '-copy-<id>' slugs and 10 numeric-ID slugs; carat variants modelled as separate URLs; 1 test product live. [STAGE 3] one PDP ranks ('marquise oval diamond', pos 90) and [STAGE 8] that SERP is PRODUCT-dominant.
current_issue: CMS IDs in slugs; variant-per-URL; test product.
notes: Flat product paths are kept (they already exist and avoid duplicate paths when a product sits in several categories). The category relationship is shown by breadcrumb and internal links, not by the path.

purpose: Single evergreen home for reference and buying-decision content.
architecture_evidence: [STAGE 11] 51 of 89 clusters (602 of 1,024 clustered keywords) are INFORMATIONAL and 14 more COMMERCIAL_RESEARCH. [STAGE 8] EDITORIAL_GUIDE is the top dominant page type (39/100); PAA 98%, AI Overview 78%. [STAGE 9] competitors rank informational content from dedicated education/guide paths (94 appearances across 10 RELEVANT domains, e.g. brilliantearth /guides/, bluenile /education/, tiffany /diamond-education/). [STAGE 10] /education exists with 1 article.
current_issue: Hub with 1 article; hub scope promises topics that do not exist [STAGE 10].
